describes: How this pack's builders laid walls of stone, by working: the sizes their stone was split or dressed to and how they laid it (the courses, the stones, the copings, the heads, the through stones, the joints, the face's batter, the top's thickness and the copings' overhang, a rebuilt panel's edges, the steps' laps and joints). The wall kind's plan stage reads it (kinds/wall.json; at R1, blender/generators/masonry.py through tools/r1_elevations.py; at R2a, the stones' part functions, blender/parts/stone/slate/stones.py and context.py, which have no defaults: a missing key is an error), by the working a wall's, a rebuilt panel's or a stair's facts name. A working names its material (materials/<id>.json), whose wear and cracking are the material's own. The wall's structure (its parapet, its stepped top, its heads, its panels' teeth) is the kind's; the rules of any wall (level beds, SN10's bond, SN2's sliver and acute limits) are code's.

notes.dry-split-1874: The gully's cheek walls as the 1874 builders laid them: split slate, dry, in level courses, the largest low. The town's own walls (docs/references/stone/ 31 and 36) are thick split slabs in level beds, big stones low. Starting values set at R1 (port step 2b), from those photographs' form and wall.py's numbers where it had them; R2b and R3 calibrate them in grey form and light. R2b lays it random coursed, as reference 10 is (tools/r2b_wall.py): always on the lowest place along the top so far, a course's height drawn smaller higher up (courseDrawPower), a stone 1.7 to 3.8 times as long as it is high, its top brought level with a neighbour's within snapMm so courses form and break, no end within bondLeastMm of a joint below; each stone set out, pitched and turned a little (setOutMm, setPitchDeg, setYawDeg), as a dry stone sits on what is under it.
notes.courseMm: A course's height. The stair's rises (146 to 188 mm here) lie one course each (R1 round 2, the coordinator's read: the town's walls are thick split slabs, so the course covers a rise); the free courses over the last step diminish to 120; the foundation courses reach 260. wall.py's 60 to 140 mm were thin flat stones, which the photographs do not show here.
notes.riseOneMm: A rise up to this is one course; over it, one line between, the lower course the larger: about 190 mm, the largest rise the coordinator's read lets one course cover.
notes.foundationMm: The courses under the foot: larger than any rise, the largest courses low (31 and 36: the biggest stone at the foot).
notes.stoneMm: A face stone's length: from 180 mm (wall.py's shortest) to 850 mm, so that SN10's 4.5 times a 190 mm course can stand (wall.py's 620 mm longest was for courses to 140 mm).
notes.drawnPerHeight: A face stone's length is drawn from 3/2 to 4/1 times its course's height (the slabs in 31 and 36 are long for their height), within stoneMm and SN10's 4.5. A draw, not a limit: the limits are SN2's sliver and SN10's 4.5, and the 139 stones R1 lays outside it are closers and cuts.
notes.shortMm: Where the geometry leaves a run no whole stones fill, the least a stone may be; every such stone is flagged in the laying's report.
notes.copeThickMm: A coping slab's thickness, split slate (wall.py's).
notes.copeNominalMm: Its nominal thickness: the ideal bed is the pitch line plus the kind's parapet less this.
notes.copeLeastMm: The least a coping slab may be where a level run or a panel leaves less than a slab; flagged.
notes.topstoneMm: A topstone's length at a wall's end, square by the kind's topstoneSquare.
notes.headTieMm: A head's tie, through the wall, as its face shows.
notes.headRunnerMm: A head's runner along one face.
notes.throughMm: A through stone's face. A dry wall is tied by through stones (docs/research/stone.md, Walls and Stones and bonding).
notes.throughFirstMm: The first through from a panel's start.
notes.throughEveryMm: And then one every 800 to 1000 mm: throughs about every 90 cm in dry double walls (docs/research/stone.md, secondary).
notes.jointMm: A joint's width between two of the wall's stones, its faces' and its copings' (SN5: 4 to 12 mm in the walls); a stone is set into its cell by a seeded half joint on each side, 2 to 6 mm. R1 lays the cells with none (the stones meet at their outlines); R2a's stones draw them (reviews/lt1/port/2b/r2a/stones/blender.md). Not the steps' tread joints, which are steps.jointMm (4 to 10 mm).
notes.batterPerHeight: How far the face leans back for its height, back then up: about one in six (SN2; wall.py's BATTER, 1/6). Only the face is cut at it; the beds stay level.
notes.topThickMm: The wall's thickness at its top, under the coping (wall.py's DEPTH, 0.42 m): a coping spans it and its overhangs, and a face stone's hidden back is half of it.
notes.copeOverMm: How much wider a standing wall's coping is than the wall's top, its overhangs on both faces together (wall.py: a standing wall's coping DEPTH + 0.05 m wide).
notes.copeProudMm: How far a coping's front stands proud of the face under it, least and most (wall.py's 15 to 35 mm); its back stands the rest of copeOverMm.
notes.copeVaryMm: How much a coping slab's thickness differs from its run's, at most: a mason picks a run's slabs to one thickness so its top runs level (R2b).
notes.copeSetDeg: How far a coping slab sits off true on the wall's top, most, [pitch, roll, yaw] in degrees: laid dry and packed, it sits a little off true, its ends never more than a few millimetres off the top (R2b).
notes.copeBedMm: How far a coping slab's bed stands over the wall's levelled top, least and most: packed tight, it touches the top course where that is level, and voids show only where the course dips (R2b, after its strict review; reference 33).
notes.topShortChance: Under a coping the top course is picked to the line; the share of its stones that fall short of it all the same (R2b, after its strict review; reference 33).
notes.topShortMm: How far a top course's stone falls short of the line under a coping, least and most: the dip pinnings pack (R2b).
notes.pinLeastMm: Under a coping the top course is brought level with flat pinnings: the least low place that takes one; a shallower one is left to the coping's bed (R2b).
notes.pinLengthMm: A pinning's length, least and most: small flat pieces of the same stone (R2b).
notes.pinGapMm: The void between two pinnings, least and most: they are wedged in where the coping rocked, not laid as a course, close enough that the slab bears on them (R2b).
notes.pinThickMm: A pinning piece's thickness, least and most: a low place is packed with a stack of thin pieces, not one block (R2b, after its strict review).
notes.pinShortMm: How far a pinning's top may fall short of the levelled top, most (R2b).
notes.steps: The stair's block steps, split slate, dry (SN3, SN5): each step's front bears lapMm on the back of the one below; a tread's joint is jointMm wide; no joint lies within jointClearMm of the joint on the step below. R2b: a tread is piecesPerTread slabs ([count, weight]; reference 06, one to three a step), none shorter than pieceLeastMm, each its rise within thickMm; a step's front line in or out by frontOutMm; settled since 1874 (the front sunk about the back's bed by settlePitchDeg, a roll of settleRollDeg, a turn of settleYawDeg, the whole down by settleDropMm: reference 06's stair that has settled). The feet keep to a walking line walkLineShare across the flight, spreading walkHalfMm about it, their wear greatest wearPeakMm back from the nosing and spreading wearSpreadMm along the tread. Moss's weights (the growth layer's): the back of each tread under the next riser (backMm deep), the ledges between laminae and the joints between a tread's pieces (reference 06's green line at the back of each tread).
notes.cement-relaid-1961: The 1961 rebuild of fl-0/r's middle (the facts' rebuilt: it bulged where the lane's water ran behind it): the wall's own stones reclaimed and relaid in cement, so its stones are the wall's working's; its own numbers are only its edges, long and short in alternate courses against the old work (wall.py's). Relaid on the wall's own line, so its joints, its batter, its top's thickness and its copings' overhang are the old work's either side (the same values as dry-split-1874's), its joints mortared within SN5's 4 to 12 mm for the walls.
